paper_title: Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners A Comprehensive   Evaluation and Beyond
caption: The evaluation matches between LLM judge and human annotations on the 300 samples.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the evaluation matches between a large language model (LLM) judge and human annotations across six categories—Correct, Rigorous, Self-aware, Active, Oriented, and No Hallucination—based on 300 samples. Each category is represented by a horizontal bar, with the total length corresponding to 100% and divided into two segments: "Matched" (in dark blue) and "Not Matched" (in light blue). The "Matched" segment dominates in all categories, indicating high agreement between the LLM judge and human annotations. The "Correct" category shows the highest match rate at 99.00%, followed closely by "No Hallucination" at 98.33% and "Oriented" at 97.33%. The "Active" category has a match rate of 97.00%, "Rigorous" at 95.33%, and "Self-aware" at 94.00%. The "Not Matched" portion is smallest in "Correct" (1.00%) and "No Hallucination" (1.67%), while "Self-aware" has the highest "Not Matched" rate at 6.00%. The bars are sorted in descending order of match rate, with the "Matched" and "Not Matched" values labeled at the end of each segment. The x-axis represents the percentage of matches, ranging from 0% to 100%, and the legend clarifies the color coding for the two segments.
